glossary.def: The EU AI Act list of use areas that make a system high-risk, such as certain decisions about people. Its rules apply from 2027-12-02 after the 2026 Omnibus.
A general-purpose AI model under the EU AI Act. Providers owe documentation, a copyright policy and a training-content summary, with extra duties for systemic-risk models.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 2026-07-27, which moved the high-risk dates and made other changes to the AI Act.
A short document accompanying a trained model that reports how it performs across conditions and states its intended use and limits.
Your own versioned document for a deployed AI system: purpose, exclusions, data and permissions, model and prompt versions, eval results, limits, oversight design and contacts.
Microsoft's document that explains how a technology works, the choices system owners can make and why to consider the whole system.
A design where a missing decision, timeout or error blocks the action instead of allowing it.
Responding to an AI incident in three stages: contain in the first hour, expand in the first 24 hours and fix at source over days or weeks, with watch periods.
A tested control that disables an agent, tool or identity quickly during an incident, for example by suspending the agent identity.
Measures that providers and deployers take so staff and others who operate AI systems understand them, required by Article 4 of the EU AI Act.

claims.text: EU AI Act Article 14 expects oversight commensurate with risk, autonomy and context: understand limits, automation-bias awareness, interpret output, decide not to use or override, and interrupt with a stop control; two competent people verify separately for Annex III point 1(a).
Article 26(2): deployers of high-risk systems assign human oversight to natural persons with the necessary competence, training, authority and support.

Meta's Agents Rule of Two (2025-10-31): within one session an agent should have no more than two of untrustworthy inputs, sensitive access and the ability to change state or communicate externally; if all three are needed, require human approval or equivalent.

In Microsoft Agent Framework Python a tool uses @tool(approval_mode="always_require") and the run result exposes user_input_requests; in .NET the function is wrapped in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction and the response carries ToolApprovalRequestContent.
By default a local approval response authorises a call only when it matches a pending request in the same AgentSession; disable_approval_response_binding opts out.
Article 12 requires high-risk systems to allow automatic recording of events over the lifetime of the system.
Article 26(6): deployers keep automatically generated logs under their control for a period appropriate to the purpose, at least six months, unless other law provides otherwise.
OWASP LLM08 recommends immutable retrieval logs among its mitigations for vector and embedding weaknesses.
In Entra Agent ID at least one sponsor is required per agent identity and blueprint; owners are optional; sponsors can disable and soft-delete, owners can also re-enable, restore and hard-delete.
The EU AI Act entered into force on 2024-08-01; prohibitions and AI literacy apply from 2025-02-02; GPAI obligations from 2025-08-02.

From 2026-08-02 Article 50 transparency rules apply and enforcement starts for GPAI, prohibitions, transparency and AI literacy; on 2026-12-02 new prohibitions apply and the Article 50(2) transition ends for systems already on the market.
The AI Omnibus moves Annex III high-risk rules to 2027-12-02 and Annex I rules to 2028-08-02.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was signed on 2026-07-08, published on 2026-07-24 and entered into force on 2026-07-27 (dates from a law-firm alert, secondary-sourced).

Article 99 fines: up to EUR 35,000,000 or 7% for prohibited practices, EUR 15,000,000 or 3% for other operator obligations, EUR 7,500,000 or 1% for incorrect information; higher figure for undertakings, lower for SMEs, and lower for small mid-caps on the 3% and 1% tiers.
Under Article 6(3) an Annex III system is not high-risk if it poses no significant risk, but profiling of natural persons is always high-risk and the provider must document the assessment.
Article 4 requires providers and deployers to support AI literacy of their staff and others operating AI systems on their behalf, without guaranteeing a specific level for any individual.
The GPAI Code of Practice was published on 2025-07-10, is voluntary and has Transparency, Copyright and Safety and Security chapters.

Article 73: serious incidents are reported within 15 days of awareness, within 2 days for a widespread infringement or Article 3(49)(b) incident, and within 10 days after a death; an incomplete initial report is allowed.
Article 73(6): the provider must not perform an investigation that alters the AI system in a way that may affect later evaluation of causes before informing the competent authorities.

Article 26(5): deployers that identify a serious incident inform the provider first, then the importer or distributor and market surveillance authorities, and suspend use where the system presents a risk.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 was released on 2023-01-26, is voluntary, has the functions Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, and NIST states it is being revised.
On 2026-04-07 NIST published a concept note for an AI RMF profile on trustworthy AI in critical infrastructure.
The NIST AI RMF Playbook gives suggested actions per sub-category, is neither a checklist nor a set of steps, and will be updated after the AI RMF is revised.
NIST AI 600-1 was released on 2024-07-26 and lists twelve risks; prompt injection and data poisoning are discussed under information security.
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is a certifiable AI management system standard run as Plan-Do-Check-Act, published December 2023, governing an organization's AI practice rather than one application.
Microsoft Responsible AI Standard v2 (June 2022) has six goal groups, includes goal A5 human oversight and control, and a Sensitive Uses review repeated at least annually (A2.3).
Microsoft Agent 365 was generally available from 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment, licensed per user, with Microsoft E5 as the best-fit prerequisite.
Agent 365 observes, governs and secures agents through the registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Entra, Purview and Defender.
Agents have no MFA and are governed with Conditional Access, which needs Microsoft 365 E7 or an Agent 365 licence with at least Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.

An Entra agent identity is a service principal without credentials of its own; the blueprint holds credentials; execution modes are S2S, OBO and Agentic-User, and Agentic-User needs the Frontier preview program.
At the 2026-05-01 Agent 365 general availability announcement, discovery of local and shadow agents through Defender and Intune was announced as preview.

Microsoft's AI incident response guidance names taxonomy gaps, context-dependent severity, ambiguous root cause and telemetry gaps, and prescribes containment in the first hour, expansion in the first 24 hours and fix at source over days or weeks, with watch periods.

Article 11: technical documentation of a high-risk system is drawn up before market placement, kept up to date, contains at least the Annex IV elements, and SMEs and small mid-caps may use a simplified form.

Article 53: GPAI providers keep technical documentation (Annex XI), give downstream providers information (Annex XII), keep a copyright policy and publish a training-content summary; the first two do not apply to open-source models unless they have systemic risk.

Article 50: people are told they interact with an AI unless obvious; synthetic output is machine-readable marked; deployers disclose deep fakes and public-interest AI text unless human-reviewed under editorial responsibility; information is clear and distinguishable at the latest at first interaction.
Microsoft Transparency Notes help system owners understand how the technology works, the choices that influence behaviour and the whole system including people and environment.
Model Cards for Model Reporting (Mitchell et al.) proposes short documents accompanying trained models; Datasheets for Datasets (Gebru et al.) is the counterpart for data.
